residencyRequirements.description: Either spouse must have been ordinarily resident in Newfoundland and Labrador for at least one year immediately before the divorce application (Divorce Act, s.3(1)).

waitingPeriod.description: No mandatory waiting period after filing. The 1-year separation must be completed before or by the time the application is granted. Divorce Order effective 31 days after made (Divorce Act, s.12).

noFault.name: One-Year Separation
noFault.description: Spouses have lived separate and apart for at least one year immediately preceding the determination of the divorce application.

fault.name: Physical or Mental Cruelty
fault.description: Respondent has treated applicant with physical or mental cruelty rendering cohabitation intolerable.

terminology.custody: Parenting Time and Decision-Making Responsibility (updated terminology per 2021 Divorce Act amendments; prior terminology: Custody and Access)
terminology.alimony: Maintenance (Newfoundland and Labrador terminology under the Family Law Act, RSNL 1990, c. F-2 — not 'spousal support')
terminology.maritalProperty: Matrimonial Property (Family Law Act, RSNL 1990, c. F-2)

basic.name: Petition for Divorce
basic.description: Initiates the divorce proceeding in the Supreme Court of Newfoundland and Labrador (Trial Division)

basic.name: Divorce Order
basic.description: Draft order to be submitted to court

effectiveDateRule: 31 days after the divorce order is made, unless the court varies the effective date or both parties waive the waiting period (Divorce Act, s.12).
certificateNote: A Certificate of Divorce may be obtained from the court office after the effective date of the Divorce Order (Divorce Act, s.12(7)).
